The passage describes brutal conditions in silver and mercury mines in Spanish colonial Peru, particularly at Huancavelica and Potosí, around 1610.  
During the period 1450–1750, silver from the Americas (especially Potosí) massively increased Spain’s wealth and financed its military ambitions, including wars in Europe.  
This silver was central to the Spanish Hapsburgs’ ability to pay for armies and conflicts across Europe and beyond.
